issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the Farm's animals collection: the UML shows animals: List<Animal> while the textual instructions (Part 3) explicitly require a Set implemented using a HashSet. The template Farm.java does not define the animals attribute, and the provided solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList). This inconsistency will confuse students about whether to use a List or a Set (and whether uniqueness/no-duplicates must be enforced), and the solution does not follow the textual requirement to use a HashSet.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent and update template/solution accordingly. Either (A) change the textual Part 3 requirement to match the UML (use a List) or (B) update the UML and the solution to require a Set<Animal> and explicitly initialize a HashSet in Farm's no-arg constructor. Also update the template Farm.java to declare the animals attribute with the chosen collection type and initialize it (e.g., private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>();), and adjust addAnimal/getter/setter/feedAllAnimals/singFarmSong implementations to operate on that collection type.

issues.description: The collection type used to hold Farm.animals is inconsistent across artifacts. The UML in the problem statement shows animals: List<Animal>, while the textual task description later requires a Set backed by a HashSet to ensure uniqueness. The solution implementation uses a List (ArrayList) for the animals attribute. This mismatch (List vs Set/HashSet) is a conceptual naming/type inconsistency that can confuse students about the required collection semantics (uniqueness) and which type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the collection type across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement UML to List<Animal> and remove the 'Set/HashSet' uniqueness requirement, or (B) change the solution (and template guidance) to use a Set<Animal> for the animals attribute and initialize it with new HashSet<>(), and update the UML in the problem statement accordingly. Prefer option B if uniqueness is intended: declare private Set<Animal> animals; initialize with new HashSet<>(); and update getters/setters to use Set<Animal>.
